nodes.name: Ti2AlC Selective Etching
nodes.procedure: 0.7 g of LiF was added to 20 mL of 6 mol/L HCl under magnetic stirring, forming a uniform solution. Then, 0.5 g of Ti2AlC powders was slowly added to the above etching solution to avoid overheating. The reaction mixture was heated to 40°C for 30 h. The resulting solid was thoroughly washed using deionized water until the pH value of the supernatant was 6-7. The final Ti2CTx MXene precipitate was freeze-dried for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: 2.1.1. Preparation of Ti2CTx... freeze-dried for 12 h.

nodes.name: Ti2CTx to MQDs Conversion
nodes.procedure: 200 mg Ti2CTx MXene was dispersed into 60 mL HCl solution (2.5 M). The solution was sonicated for 3 h under Ar atmosphere protection. Next, the mixture was agitated at room temperature for 72 h (Ar atmosphere) at 600 rpm magnetic stirring speed. The supernatant was collected by centrifugation at 11000 rpm for 30 min, then filtered through 0.22 μm microporous filter membrane until no residue remained.

unit_operations.name: Dispersion
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: 200 mg Ti2CTx MXene was dispersed into 60 mL HCl solution (2.5 M). And then, the solution was sonicated for 3 h under the protection of Ar atmosphere.

unit_operations.name: Etching
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the mixture was agitated at room temperature for 72 h (Ar atmosphere). Moreover, the speed of magnetic stirring was 600 rpm.

unit_operations.name: Purification
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the supernatant was collected by centrifugation at 11000 rpm, for 30 min. To further remove the larger nanoparticles, the supernatant was filtered by a 0.22 μm microporous filter membrane until there was no residue on the membrane.

nodes.source_text: 2.1.2. Preparation of Ti2C Tx MQDs... until there was no residue on the membrane.

nodes.name: Co Foam Pre-treatment
nodes.procedure: Co foam (1 cm × 1 cm projected area) was cleaned sequentially by ultrasonication in 0.5 M HCl, acetone, and ethanol for 5 min each, then dried under vacuum at 60°C overnight.

unit_operations.name: Sequential Cleaning
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: cleaned by 0.5 M HCl, acetone, and ethanol by ultrasonication for 5 min, respectively

unit_operations.name: Vacuum Drying
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: dried in a vacuum overnight at 60°C

nodes.source_text: Firstly, the Co foam was cleaned by 0.5 M HCl, acetone, and ethanol... projected area of Co foam was controlled to be 1 cm × 1 cm.

nodes.name: MQDs/Co2(OH)3Cl Pre-catalyst Formation
nodes.procedure: Cleaned Co foam was immersed in MQDs solution (optimized at 9 h immersion) to form MQDs/Co2(OH)3Cl via electrostatic self-assembly in acidic HCl environment, then dried at 60°C for 12 h. The acidic environment with Cl- ions led to chemical reaction forming Co2(OH)3Cl on Co foam surface.
nodes.source_text: Co foam was immersed in MQDs solution for 2 h, 4 h, 6 h, 9 h... dried in a drying oven at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Co2(OH)3Cl Control Pre-catalyst
nodes.procedure: Control sample synthesized using identical procedure as MQDs version but HCl solution without MQDs. Cl- in acidic environment accelerates Co corrosion and oxidation to form Co2(OH)3Cl.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of Co2(OH)3Cl/Co foam: The control sample was synthesized by the above same method. However, the HCl solution did not contain MQDs.

nodes.name: Electrochemical Phase Conversion
nodes.procedure: For electrochemical conversion from Co2(OH)3Cl to β-Co(OH)2, a current density of 10 mA cm^-2 was applied for 3 h.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of QDs/Co(OH)2/Co foam: For electrochemical conversion from Co2(OH)3Cl to β-Co(OH)2, a current density of 10 mA cm^-2 was applied for 3 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern confirmed the hexagonal structure of the Co₂(OH)₃Cl catalyst (PDF#97-015-5534), with the (101) peaks shifting slightly from 16.03° to 15.98° upon the introduction of Ti₂CTₓ MQDs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern confirmed the hexagonal structure of the Co₂(OH)₃Cl [28] catalyst (PDF#97-015-5534), with the (101) peaks shifting slightly from 16.03° to 15.98° upon the introduction of Ti₂CTₓ MQDs (Fig. 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES peak for the MQDs/Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF catalyst exhibited higher energy than that for the control catalyst, implying that MQD caused a higher oxidation state of Co.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K-edge XANES peak for the MQDs/Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF catalyst exhibited higher energy than did that for the control catalyst, implying that MQD caused a higher oxidation state of Co.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR revealed distinct bending vibration peaks of Co-OH (3552 cm⁻¹) and O-Co-O bonds (421 cm⁻¹); introduction of MQDs resulted in a shift in the vibration position of the Co-OH bond.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy revealed distinct bending vibration peaks of Co-OH 3552 cm⁻¹) and O-Co-O bonds (421 cm⁻¹) (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows MQDs/Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF after 3h reaction forms regular hexagonal nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images show the irregular morphology gradually evolves into regular hexagonal nanosheets after reaction 3h (Fig. S14 and Fig. 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows MQDs lateral size 2-4.5 nm; β-Co(OH)₂ hexagonal nanosheets with MQDs (~3 nm); lattice fringes 0.22 nm (103) Ti₂CTₓ and 0.28 nm (100) Co(OH)₂; dislocations in Co(OH)₂ lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the MQDs/Co(OH)₂ nanosheet was characterized through transmission electron microscopy (TEM)... lattice fringe spacings of 0.22 and 0.28 nm matched the d-spacings for the (103) lattice of Ti₂CTₓ MQDs and the (100) plane of Co(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Co2p XPS shows Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio of 0.58 for MQDs/Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF-R vs 0.62 for control after reaction, indicating higher chemical states of Co (Co²⁺δ); Ti2p shows negative shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to the Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF-R sample (Co²⁺/Co³⁺ = 0.62), the lower Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio (Co²⁺/Co³⁺ = 0.58) of MQDs/Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF-R suggests that an interaction between the MQDs and the generated Co(OH)₂ holds higher chemical states of Co (Co²⁺δ).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra showed a blue shift of approximately 10 cm⁻¹ in the Co-Cl vibration mode for MQDs/Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF compared with Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman Spectra of the MQDs/Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF catalyst showed a blue shift of approximately 10 cm⁻¹ in the Co-Cl vibration mode compared with the Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF catalyst (Fig. S13).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV used to calculate Cdl and ECSA=240 cm⁻² for MQDs/Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF-R catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical surface area (ECSA) is a key parameter... The MQDs/Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF-R catalyst outperformed the Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF-R catalyst in terms of ECSA, achieving a value of 240 cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance of 4.514 Ω for MQDs catalyst vs 55.9 Ω for control.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nyquist plots indicated that the MQDs/Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF-R catalyst had a considerably lower charge transfer resistance (4.514 Ω) than those of the CF (555 Ω) and Co₂(OH)₃Cl/CF-R (55.9 Ω) catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS line scanning shows uniform Ti and Co distribution on β-Co(OH)₂ nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The distribution of MQDs on the surface of β-Co(OH)₂ nanosheets was further examined through energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy line scanning coupled with HAADF-STEM (Fig. 2f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Soft X-ray emission spectroscopy (SXES) shows the fast leaching of Cl⁻ from Co₂(OH)₃Cl is central to the formation of β-Co(OH)₂ nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Soft X-ray emission spectroscopy (SXES) shows the fast leaching of Cl⁻ from Co₂(OH)₃Cl is central to the formation of β-Co(OH)₂ nanosheets (Fig. S22).

nodes.characterization_summary: Time-of-flight secondary-ion mass spectrometry detects Ti signals confirming MQDs distribution on β-Co(OH)₂ nanosheet surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Time-of-flight secondary-ion mass spectrometry [36] was employed for detecting the Ti signals of the nanosheet (Fig. 2g).
